title: Vibe-triggered Ozi auto-execute mode on wakeup
description: When a vibe is chosen at wakeup, Ozi scores the backlog, presents a ranked plan, and executes autonomously — the user does not sequence work. Ozi stops when: context hits 50%, work queue is empty, or remaining items require user input/decisions. Skipping vibe preserves current passive behavior.
perceive: Read wai.md Step 9. Vibe currently just stores a value and shows the wakeup banner — no auto-execution. User sessions are primarily for refinement/direction; build is Tender's job. When a vibe is chosen, the user expects Ozi to take over, not wait.
execute: Edit wai.md Step 9 to: (1) distinguish vibe-chosen vs skipped paths; (2) add Step 9b — Ozi auto-execute loop with score, plan, execute, stop-condition checks. Stop conditions: context ≥50%, queue empty, next item needs-user-input. Needs-user-input detection: missing PEV, type=decision/idea/policy, description keywords (browser/credential/oauth/deploy/login/manual/physical). Show 5s countdown before executing. Report inline per item. Surface blocked items as batch at end.
verify: Read wai.md and confirm: (1) vibe-chosen path leads to Step 9b, (2) vibe-skipped path leads to banner+wait, (3) stop conditions are enumerated, (4) needs-user-input detection is specified, (5) plan display format and inline reporting format are present.
acceptance_criteria: wai.md Step 9 has two paths: vibe-chosen → Step 9b auto-execute; skipped → banner+wait
Step 9b specifies score+rank using score_backlog.py with vibe arg
Plan display shown before execution with 5s countdown
Execute loop with per-item stop condition checks
Stop conditions: context ≥50%, queue empty, needs-user-input
Paused items surfaced as batch with reasons after queue or stop
